strings: Used to copy important documents and anatomy studies.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
A canister for the storage of gas.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
If you want to get cancer, might as well do it in style.
This is the adorable by-product of multiple attempts at genetically mixing mothpeople with cockroaches.
Now you see me, now you don't...
A shield generator meant for use in xenobiology.
A sign that warns of dangerous particulates or gasses in the air, instructing you to wear internals.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.

An industrial unit made to hold, charge, and decontaminate equipment. It comes with a built-in UV cauterization mechanism. A small warning label advises that organic matter should not be placed into the unit.
A large vessel containing pressurized gas.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
From BlenderTech. Will It Blend? Let's test it out!
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
A heavy wooden box, which can be filled with a lot of ores or boulders
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
It's a secure locker for personnel. The first person to swipe their ID gains control.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
A low-end laptop often used for personal recreation.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
A structure built out of bricks, for heating up metal, or glass, or ceramic, or food, or anything really.
Someone's gotten on the naughty list.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A long list of rules to be followed when in the library, extolling the virtues of being quiet at all times and threatening those who would dare eat hot food inside.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
A vivarium in which aquatic fauna and flora are usually kept and displayed.
A refillable can that dispenses nutritious fish feed.
A special circuit imprinter with a built in interface meant for departmental usage, with built in ExoSync receivers allowing it to print designs researched that match its ROM-encoded department type.
A console that will ping when a positronic personality is available for download.
A beacon used by a teleporter.
Well, the flow of time is normal on these tiles, weird.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Medbay is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Science department is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Security department is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Command department is.
A medical wrench with common(medical?) uses. Can be found in your hand.
Pricy sterile gloves that are thicker than latex. Excellent grip ensures very fast carrying of patients along with the faster use time of various chemical related items.
A device that delivers powerful shocks to detachable paddles that resuscitate incapacitated patients. 	Has a rear bracket for attachments to wall mounts and medical cyborgs.
A first aid kit with the ability to heal common types of injuries.
A roll of elastic cloth, perfect for stabilizing all kinds of wounds, from cuts and burns, to broken bones.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
It's a storage unit for fire-fighting supplies.
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
A small crowbar. This handy tool is useful for lots of things, such as prying floor tiles or opening unpowered doors.
A basic handheld radio that communicates with local telecommunication networks.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
The HS-452. Installed in the 2550s by the Nanotrasen Hygiene Division, now with 2560 lead compliance! Passively replenishes itself with water when not in use.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
The banner of the eternal Cargonia, with the mystical power of conjuring any object into existence.
The HU-452, an experimental urinal. Comes complete with experimental urinal cake.
A Prism-brand path illumination device. It is anchored in place and glowing steadily.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
A bottle with a sharp broken bottom.
A bottle of rotgut. Its owner has applied some street wisdom to cleverly disguise it as a brown paper bag.
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
A combined label printer, applicator, and remover, all in a single portable device. Designed to be easy to operate and use.
A headset for the trained staff of the medbay.
Mirror mirror on the wall, who's the most robust of them all?
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
A compact, high resolution scanning module used in the construction of certain devices.
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.
The official corporate flag of Nanotrasen. Mostly flown as a ceremonial piece, or to mark land on a new frontier.
A figurine depicting the one-and-only Curator.
A device that analyzes a slime's internal composition and measures its stats.
A dropper. Holds up to 5 units.
A crafting bench fitted with tools, securing mechanisms, and a steady surface for blacksmithing.
A billow specifically crafted for use in forging. Used to stoke the flames and keep the forge lit.
A set of tongs specifically crafted for use in forging. A wise man once said 'I lift things up and put them down.'
A mallet specifically crafted for use in forging. Used to slowly shape metal; careful, you could break something with it!
A tree straight from the tropics.
A one meter section of heat-exchanging pipe.
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
box of smart metal foam grenades
Used to rapidly seal hull breaches. This variety conforms to the walls of its area.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
A device that can edit nanite program disks to adjust their functionality.
A combined blastdoor and mass driver control unit.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A telescreen that connects to the AI upload's camera network.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images. This one will refuse to auto-connect incoming calls.
A board for pinning important notices upon. It is made of the finest Spanish cork.
Due to various fly related incident, management has disabled direct control of this console.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A radio beacon used for bot navigation.
Use this to keep prisoners in line.
Gets rid of those pesky bloodstains, or your money back!
Uses patented retractable wheel technology. Never sacrifice speed for style - not that this provides much of either.
The height of fashion, and they're pre-polished!
A more portable sort of aquarium to store various fishes in, unless they're too big or there're too many of them.
A pair of snazzy goggles used to protect against chemical spills. Fitted with an analyzer for scanning items and reagents.
It's a storage unit for emergency breath masks and O2 tanks.
